svg.title: Warp divergence, from where it comes: an SPH dam break of 260 particles plays out; one warp of 32 neighbouring particles is taken from it, each a GPU thread gathering the neighbours inside its kernel radius; their real neighbour counts (5 to 14) become the work, and the warp steps in lockstep for 14 steps with 20.0 of 32 lanes busy on average, the rest masked off. Measured on a million particles: 33.34% branch efficiency, and still faster, 158.87 against 153.13 GB/s.

g.text: SPH DAM BREAK, AS IN OPENFPM · 5× SLOWER

svg.text: A third of the efficiency, and still faster · 158.87 vs 153.13 GB/s, 1M particles
